newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia hopes U.N. embargo on Iraq lifted this year.
newsitem.headline: Russia hopes U.N. embargo on Iraq lifted this year.

text.p: Russia hopes that U.N. sanctions against Iraq will be lifted this year and Moscow will send an energy delegation to Baghdad soon to discuss post-embargo oil ties, Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov said on Wednesday.

Primakov spoke at a joint press conference with Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz, who has won Moscow's support for lifting stiff sanctions imposed by the United Nations against Iraq after Baghdad invaded Kuwait in 1990.
"We hope that this year all limitations...on the export of Iraqi oil will be lifted," Primakov said.

He said Russia supported a permanent extension of an oil-for-food deal with the United Nations that allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to raise cash for food and medicine. The deal began in December, 1996.
Under the 1991 Gulf War ceasefire terms, limits on Iraqi oil exports can be lifted only if the U.N. Special Commission testifies that Baghdad has completely fulfilled all its disarmament obligations.
"In April, a half-year accounting by the (U.N. arms monitoring) commission will take place and we hope at this time, or just after this, any remaining questions will be removed," Primakov said.
He said that Russia was eager to see its relationship with Iraq develop and that a Russian energy delegation would discuss cooperation.
"It is imagined that these negotiations will give a certain impulse to our relations that will develop after the removal of the embargo," he said.

In the oil-for-food deal, seven Russian companies are contracted to lift a total of 25.2 million barrels, at 140,000 barrels per day (bpd), over six months from Iraq's outlets at Ceyhan on the Turkish Mediterranean and its Gulf port of Mina al-Bakr.
